english.notes:
(i) Any motor vehicle, bicycle or other conveyance used, left or placed in breach of this byelaw may be removed and stored, by or under the direction of an Operator or authorised person (byelaw 14A(4)). It may also be removed and stored by such persons where the operator or authorised person reasonably believes doing so is necessary to deal with an emergency, to allow access to persons or vehicles to enable maintenance of the railway to be carried out; or to enable the safe and efficient operation of the railway (byelaw 14A(5)).
(ii) Byelaw 24(2) provides a power for authorised person to remove persons from the railway. See Byelaw 23(1) for the associated power to require a name and address.
(iii) Schedule 2 to the Railway Byelaws provides that in byelaw 25(1) the following operators are excluded from the definition of operator; Great Central Railway (Nottingham) Limited, London Underground Limited Tube Lines Limited and Tyne and Wear Passenger Transport Executive.
(iv) This offence applies from the 25th December 2025 due to changes made by the Railway Byelaws Amendment Order 2025. For the offences applying before this date, see offences H8072, H8073, H8074 and H8075.
(v) The Railway Byelaws 2005 were made by the Strategic Rail Authority under section 219 of the Transport Act 2000 and confirmed under Schedule 20 to the Transport Act 2000, both of which were repealed on 15th October 2015. Section 46(4) of the Railways Act 2005 provides that these Byelaws remain in force.
